summary: The candidate is correct and self-contained. Each unordered pair has inclusion probability 1/(N-1) for even N and 1/N for odd N, yielding the stated unweighted and weighted expectations. Both variance identities and the pointwise minimum-weight inequality are valid, the factor-K bounds follow with the correct parity constants, and the equality and attainment claims include the necessary equal-weight hypothesis. The quotient norm is well defined because every subspace of finite-dimensional Euclidean space is closed, and disjoint edge label sets give the claimed global disjointness while allowing the deterministic lower bounds to be summed.
